findings.reason: naming the test-side window removes §37's second repair branch and its follower-module write path, so the node is not sent hunting a product defect its evidence rules out.
findings.text: §37's Why claims the two windows are indistinguishable, but a miss inside the read loop (the follower-defect window) leaves the test's `_wait_for` predicate unsatisfied for its whole ceiling — `WATCHER_LOAD_BOUND_SECONDS = 30.0` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:48`), the default at `tests/test_removed_flag_migration.py:381` — and would fail at the `pytest.fail` inside `_wait_for`, not at the set assertion; all three cited failing runs instead fail at the line-446 set assertion below that ceiling (base `repeat-base2-removed_flag.log` runs 1 and 4 at 21.49 s and 22.81 s; head `repeat-head2-removed_flag.log` run 2 at 21.25 s), which requires the predicate to have been satisfied, i.e. the reader read the fleet in its post-move state — the test-side window — so the follower window is already excluded by §37's own cited logs

response_events.reason: §37 has the node confirm the window before repairing; the cited failures stopping at the set assertion below the wait ceiling are evidence it will read, and an unused follower branch costs nothing

reasoning-1.reason: §37 has the node confirm the window before repairing; the cited failures stopping at the set assertion below the wait ceiling are evidence it will read, and an unused follower branch costs nothing

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `repeat-base2-removed_flag.log` and `repeat-head2-removed_flag.log` resolve; base `6d186434` and head `98616e44` are both commits; `tests/test_removed_flag_migration.py` and `cli._follow_watch_lines` resolve (`reckon/cli.py:335` re-exporting `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1757`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §37's Done-when carries a named negative control ("reintroduces the window, by moving the pointers before the reader attaches"), a sibling-case clause ("the other cases in `tests/test_removed_flag_migration.py` still pass") and a per-run rate (20 of 20 alone, 10 of 10 under `-n 8`), all of which can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — logs are required "under the run directory" with revision, literal command and a trailing `EXIT=`; the two cited logs exist on disk under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261021T204353308966-the-pane-repeats-no-line-that-carries-no-news/`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach the test file or the follower module, and §37's prose describes the mechanism (a reader attaching before the fixture moves) rather than a tracker entry.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §37's Why says the two candidate windows "the evidence so far does not tell them apart", but the logs it cites do discriminate, and the undecided branch points the node at a product defect its own evidence excludes.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, "make the delivery test deliver every state deterministically", closed on one verdict; the fix location is left to the node's evidence, not made a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §37 declares no `depends-on`/`informs`/`gates` and needs none; its only shared write path, `tests/test_removed_flag_migration.py`, is also §28's, but §28 is `done` (`plan-section-declarations`), so no ordering constraint is left unstated.
